summary: Part 2 of the Nike deep dive (published 2026-09-19) explains why investors are focused on Nike: it sits at a 52-week low and is down enormously from its ~$175 high, while the turnaround is taking longer than hoped. The creator recounts having warned against the stock at every price level ($175 down through $45) over five years, then finally upgrading it to a buy at ~$40 — since which it has fallen to ~$36, making it even more attractive. Nike's revival strategy centers on refreshing 15,000+ wholesale display spaces globally and discounting less on Nike Digital to rebuild wholesaler trust (wholesalers won't stock products they see undercut online). Management repeatedly stressed 'at our scale, this is going to take time.' His biggest risk concern is that he was early: fundamentals remain weak — excess unwanted inventory, especially in China, forcing heavy discounting that cannibalizes full-price new releases, plus macro headwinds on discretionary spending. He's 'kicking the tires' on a personal entry and is considering selling put options at $32 or $30 strikes. Call: NKE BUY (upgraded to buy at ~$40; now ~$36, even more attractive).
